name: Kaluki (South Africa)
description: Kaluki (South African version) is a high-penalty variant of Rummy popular in South Africa. Played with two decks and four Jokers, it is distinguished by its severe scoring systemâ€”Jokers are worth 50 penalty pointsâ€”which forces players to prioritize safety and risk management over aggressive melding. It is typically a 7-round game with fixed 13-card hands.

history.origins: Likely evolved from British Kalooki rules brought to South Africa by Commonwealth connections. It developed a more 'punishing' scoring profile to discourage hoarding wild cards.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Rummy gains popularity in Johannesburg and Cape Town socials.
1970s: The 50-point Joker rule becomes a standard 'South African' convention.
Present: A very common household and club game, often played during weekend gatherings.
history.cultural: In South Africa, Kaluki is often played alongside other family classics like 'Hearts' or 'Canasta', with an emphasis on social banter and quick turns.
history.evolution: The game moved away from complex contract sequences toward a consistent, high-speed melding format where the focus is on finishing the round as quickly as possible.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards. The rest go to the stock.
setup.equipment: Standard cards, score sheet, chips for stakes (optional).

rules.objective: Be the first to 'Go Out' by melding all cards. The player with the lowest score after 7 rounds is the champion.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Drawing**: Each turn, draw either the top card of the stock or the top discard. 2. **Melding**: Form sets (3-4 cards same rank) and runs (3+ consecutive same suit). 3. **Initial Meld**: Must meet round-specific point requirements. 4. **Discarding**: End turn by discarding one card.
keyRules: 7 rounds with different initial meld requirements each round
Sets: 3-4 cards of same rank (different suits preferred)
Runs: 3+ consecutive cards of same suit
Jokers are wild cards. Can represent any card
WARNING: Holding a Joker when someone else goes out is a 50-point penalty
Once you have made your first meld, you can add your cards to ANY existing meld on the table
Red Aces count as 1 point (low penalty), Black Aces count as 15 points

strategy.basic: Priority: Get rid of Jokers! Because they are 50 points, it is almost never worth holding onto a Joker to complete a long run. Play it as soon as you have a valid set.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Red Ace' Strategy: If you suspect another player is about to go out, try to hoard Red Aces. They only count as 1 point, allowing you to 'lose' the round with minimal damage.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: Pay attention to what cards are being picked up from the discard pile. If you know an opponent needs a 7 of Hearts to go out, keep that 7 in your hand even if it doesn't help your own meld.
tips: Black Aces are high value (15) but also help hit opening requirements if your house uses themâ€”check your point values before playing.
In South African play, 'Going Out' is the only priority. Don't worry about 'perfect' melds.

scoring.description: Winner of a round scores 0. Losers score penalty points for cards remaining in hand. Game played over 7 rounds.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest total points after 7 rounds wins. Players exceeding 150 penalty points may be eliminated.

synthesis.shortDescription: A high-stakes South African rummy variant where Jokers carry a devastating 50-point penalty. Master the 7-round structure and manage your risk to emerge victorious.
